  • Configuration — configure providers and tiers from the Settings workspace
  • Certificates & Compliance — interpret the certificate status panel
  • Continuous Monitoring — feed the dashboard with ongoing drift detection

docs.title: Docker & Deployment
docs.text: CHERENKOV ships with Docker Compose files for running the full stack locally or in production. The Dockerfile builds a multi-stage image that includes the React UI, Python engine, and Playwright browsers.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa.git
cd cherenkov-qa

# Start the full stack (Prism mock + CHERENKOV)
docker compose up -d

# Start with Ollama and full LLM pipeline
docker compose --profile full up -d

# Start with demo mode dashboard
docker compose --profile demo up -d

Open http://localhost:8000 for the dashboard (demo profile) or http://localhost:4010 for the Prism mock server.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph "docker-compose.yml"
        P[Prism Mock Server\n:4010]
        C[CHERENKOV Engine]
        O[Ollama\n:11434]
        OI[Ollama Init\nPulls models]
        D[CHERENKOV Demo\n:8000]
    end

    subgraph "docker-compose.ai.yml"
        L[LocalAI\n:8080]
        R[Redis\n:6379]
        CA[CHERENKOV AI Stack\n:8000 + :8001]
    end

    C --> P
    C --> O
    OI --> O
    CA --> L
    CA --> R

    style C fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
    style CA fill:#db2777,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff

docs.title: docker-compose.yml — Core Stack
docs.text:
The default compose file provides:

Service Image Port Profile Purpose prism stoplight/prism:5 4010 default OpenAPI mock server cherenkov Built from Dockerfile — default Core validation engine ollama ollama/ollama 11434 full Local LLM server ollama-init curlimages/curl — full Pulls required models on startup cherenkov-demo Built from Dockerfile 8000 demo Dashboard with sample data 
# Core only (Prism + CHERENKOV engine)
docker compose up -d

# Full stack with Ollama
docker compose --profile full up -d

# Demo dashboard
docker compose --profile demo up -d

docs.title: docker-compose.ai.yml — AI Stack
docs.text:
A separate compose file for running the AI infrastructure (LocalAI + Redis) alongside CHERENKOV:

Service Image Port Purpose local-ai localai/localai:latest-cpu 8080 OpenAI-compatible local inference redis redis:7-alpine 6379 Caching and queue persistence cherenkov Built from Dockerfile 8000, 8001 Engine with full AI + monitoring 
# Start the AI stack
docker compose -f docker-compose.ai.yml up -d

This stack pre-configures CHERENKOV with:

  • LocalAI as the LLM provider (OpenAI-compatible API)
  • Redis for caching and persistent divergence queues
  • Monitoring enabled on port 8001

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
The Dockerfile uses a multi-stage build:

Stage 1 — UI Build:

  • Base: node:26-slim
  • Builds the React dashboard UI with Vite

Stage 2 — Engine:

  • Base: python:3.14-slim
  • Installs system dependencies (curl, git, Node.js)
  • Installs the Python package in editable mode
  • Installs Playwright with Chromium
  • Copies the built UI from stage 1
  • Runs as a non-root cherenkov user (UID 1000)
  • Health check against /health endpoint
# Build the image directly
docker build -t cherenkov-qa .

# Run a one-off validation
docker run --rm cherenkov-qa validate \
  --spec /specs/openapi.yaml \
  --target http://host.docker.internal:8080

docs.title: Environment Variables for Docker
docs.text:
Pass environment variables to configure CHERENKOV inside Docker:

services:
  cherenkov:
    build: .
    environment:
      # LLM provider — point to a Docker service
      - OLLAMA_URL=http://ollama:11434/api/generate
      - PROVIDER=ollama
      - GEN_MODEL=qwen2.5-coder:7b

      # VLM
      - CHERENKOV_VLM_PROVIDER=ollama
      - CHERENKOV_VLM_LOCALAI_URL=http://local-ai:8080

      # Redis
      - CHERENKOV_REDIS_ENABLED=true
      - CHERENKOV_REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379/0

      # Monitoring
      - CHERENKOV_MONITORING_ENABLED=true
      - CHERENKOV_METRICS_PORT=8001

      # Network
      - CHERENKOV_EGRESS=internal
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"   # Dashboard
      - "8001:8001"   # Metrics
    volumes:
      - ./.cherenkov:/app/.cherenkov   # Persist state across restarts

See the Configuration reference for all available environment variables.

docs.title: GPU Support
docs.text:
For GPU-accelerated inference with Ollama:

services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: 1
              capabilities: [gpu]
    volumes:
      - ollama_models:/root/.ollama

GPU is optional

CHERENKOV runs on CPU by default. GPU acceleration significantly speeds up LLM generation but is not required. The default qwen2.5-coder:7b model works well on CPU with ~4GB RAM.

docs.title: Persistent Storage
docs.text:
Mount volumes for state that should survive container restarts:

volumes:
  - ./.cherenkov:/app/.cherenkov     # HITL queue, guardian DB, run history
  - ./output:/app/output             # Reports and certificates
  - ollama_models:/root/.ollama      # Downloaded models (avoid re-pulling)

docs.title: Health Checks
docs.text:
The CHERENKOV container includes a built-in health check:

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD python -c "import urllib.request; urllib.request.urlopen('http://localhost:8000/health', timeout=5)" || exit 1

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• The container runs as a non-root user (cherenkov, UID 1000)
  • Set CHERENKOV_EGRESS=none for air-gapped environments
  • Use CHERENKOV_EGRESS=internal to allow LAN-only traffic (e.g., to Ollama in another container)

docs.title: Scaling
docs.text:
For high-throughput environments, run the engine and dashboard as separate services:

services:
  engine:
    build: .
    command: ["daemon", "--url", "http://api:8080", "--interval", "30"]
    # No ports exposed — headless

  dashboard:
    build: .
    command: ["dashboard"]
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
For Kubernetes deployment, see the K8s Operator guide. The operator provides:

  • Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) for CHERENKOV workloads
  • Automatic scaling based on queue depth
  • Helm chart for standard deployments

docs.title: Eject to Vanilla Playwright
docs.text: cherenkov eject is your zero lock-in guarantee. Run it at any time to strip all CHERENKOV dependencies from your generated tests, leaving pure, human-readable Playwright tests that run forever — with no CHERENKOV installed.

docs.title: Run the Eject Command
docs.text:
cherenkov eject --output ./my-tests

This takes every test in your CHERENKOV workspace and transforms it:

Before (CHERENKOV test): 

import { createCherenkovClient } from '@cherenkov/client';
import { validateResponse } from '@cherenkov/validate';

test('GET /pets returns 200', async ({ request }) => {
  const client = createCherenkovClient({ baseUrl: process.env.API_URL });
  const res = await client.get('/pets');
  validateResponse(res, petSchema);
  expect(res.status).toBe(200);
});

After (ejected vanilla Playwright): 

import createClient from 'openapi-fetch';
import type { paths } from './generated-types';

test('GET /pets returns 200', async ({ request }) => {
  const client = createClient<paths>({ baseUrl: process.env.API_URL });
  const { data, response } = await client.GET('/pets');
  expect(response.status).toBe(200);
  expect(data).toBeDefined();
});

docs.title: Run Ejected Tests
docs.text:
cd my-tests
npm install
npx playwright test

# All tests pass — no CHERENKOV required

docs.title: What Gets Removed
docs.text: Removed Replaced With @cherenkov/client import openapi-fetch (standard) @cherenkov/validate import Inline assertions CHERENKOV-specific type helpers Generated openapi-typescript types CHERENKOV config file references Standard Playwright config

docs.title: What Stays
docs.text:
• Test logic and assertions — unchanged
  • TypeScript type safety — via openapi-fetch + openapi-typescript
  • Playwright fixtures and configuration
  • Your .env and base URL configuration

docs.title: Eject Strategy
docs.text:
When to eject

  • Before migrating to a new test framework
  • Before archiving a project
  • When handing tests to a team that doesn't use CHERENKOV
  • As a periodic "test ownership audit"

CHERENKOV recommends ejecting periodically to verify that your tests don't have hidden CHERENKOV dependencies.

docs.title: Verify Portability
docs.text:
# Confirm no CHERENKOV imports remain
grep -r "@cherenkov" ./my-tests
# Expected: no output

# Run without CHERENKOV installed
pip uninstall cherenkov-qa
cd my-tests && npx playwright test
# Expected: all tests pass

docs.title: Human-in-the-Loop Workflow
docs.text:
CHERENKOV generates test findings and conformance decisions using AI, but not every AI decision is trustworthy. The Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) system routes low-confidence findings to human reviewers for final judgment.

Design invariant (D7): CHERENKOV never auto-edits your code. Every change is a suggestion that a human approves or rejects.

docs.title: Why HITL Matters
docs.text:
AI models hallucinate. A conformance test might flag a "divergence" that is actually a valid API behavior the model misunderstood. Or a generated test might weaken an assertion without anyone noticing. The HITL queue catches these cases.

flowchart TD
    A[AI generates finding] --> B{Confidence >= 90%?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Auto-approve]
    B -->|No| D{Confidence >= 70%?}
    D -->|Yes| E["HITL Queue\n(human review)"]
    D -->|No| F[Auto-reject]

    E --> G[Human: Approve]
    E --> H[Human: Reject + reason]

    C --> I[Applied to suite]
    G --> I
    H --> J[Discarded with audit trail]
    F --> J

    style E fill:#db2777,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
    style A fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff

docs.title: HITL Queue Lifecycle
docs.text:
Each finding enters the queue as pending and moves to one of three terminal states:

Status Meaning pending Waiting for human review approved Human confirmed the finding is valid rejected Human dismissed the finding with a reason ignored Deprioritized — may revisit later

docs.title: List pending items
docs.text:
cherenkov hitl list

Output:

  e1a2b3c4-...  pending     sev=high      conf=0.78  gate=prism_dry_run  GET /pets/{petId}
  f5d6e7a8-...  pending     sev=medium    conf=0.72  gate=meaningful     POST /pets

Filter by status:

cherenkov hitl list --status approved
cherenkov hitl list --status rejected

docs.title: Show item details
docs.text:
cherenkov hitl show e1a2b3c4-...

Displays full details: endpoint, mutation, confidence score, confidence reason, review gate that failed, and timestamps.

docs.title: Approve a finding
docs.text:
cherenkov hitl approve e1a2b3c4-...

The item moves to approved and is attributed to the current $USER.

docs.title: Reject a finding
docs.text:
cherenkov hitl reject f5d6e7a8-... --reason "API correctly returns 404 for unknown pet IDs"

Always provide a reason — it becomes part of the audit trail and helps the AI learn from its mistakes.

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
Every HITL command supports --json for machine-readable output:

cherenkov hitl list --json | jq '.payload.items[] | .id'

The JSON follows the hitl/v1 envelope schema:

{
  "schema_version": "hitl/v1",
  "ok": true,
  "command": "list",
  "payload": {
    "items": [...]
  },
  "error": null
}

docs.title: Dashboard Triage Workspace
docs.text:
The Triage workspace in the dashboard provides a visual Kanban board for HITL review:

  1. Launch the dashboard: cherenkov dashboard
  2. Navigate to Triage (third tab)
  3. Drag findings between columns: Pending, Approved, Rejected
  4. Click a finding to see full details, including the generated test code and the divergence evidence
  5. Approve or Reject with one click — bulk actions available for batch processing

docs.title: Severity Levels
docs.text:
Findings are classified by severity. Higher severity items appear first in the queue.

Severity Meaning Example critical API is broken in a way that affects all consumers Auth endpoint returns 500 high Significant spec divergence Required field missing from response medium Non-critical divergence Response includes undocumented field low Minor or cosmetic Different header casing

docs.title: Audit Trail
docs.text:
Every HITL decision is recorded in an SQLite audit log (.cherenkov/hitl.db) with:

  • command — the action taken (approve, reject, ignore)
  • actor — who made the decision (from $USER or dashboard auth)
  • item_id — the finding being acted on
  • outcome — the result (ok, conflict, not_found)
  • timestamp — when the action occurred

Query the audit trail:

cherenkov hitl list --status approved --json | jq '.payload.items[] | {id, approved_by, approved_at}'

docs.title: CI gate: require zero pending items
docs.text:
# In your CI pipeline — fail if any findings need human review
pending=$(cherenkov hitl list --json | jq '.payload.items | length')
if [ "$pending" -gt 0 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: $pending findings need human review before merge"
  exit 1
fi

docs.title: Daemon mode: auto-feed the queue
docs.text:
When running cherenkov daemon, new divergences are automatically added to the HITL queue. Reviewers can triage them throughout the day via the dashboard.

cherenkov daemon --url http://staging:8080 &
cherenkov dashboard  # Triage incoming findings in real time

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Dashboard & UI — navigate the Triage workspace
  • Test Generation & Repair — understand what generates the findings HITL reviews
  • Certificates & Compliance — HITL decisions feed into certification verdicts
  • Continuous Monitoring — HITL queue as a real-time divergence inbox

docs.title: Kubernetes Operator
docs.text: CHERENKOV ships a Kubernetes operator that manages ConformanceCheck custom resources for scheduled, in-cluster API conformance runs. The operator is built with controller-runtime and runs as a Deployment in the cherenkov namespace.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  K8s API Server                         │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ ConformanceCheck CR (validation │    │
│  │ .cherenkov.io/v1alpha1)         │    │
│  └──────────┬──────────────────────┘    │
└─────────────┼───────────────────────────┘
              │ reconcile
┌─────────────▼───────────────────────────┐
│  cherenkov-operator (Deployment)        │
│  - Watches ConformanceCheck resources   │
│  - Creates Jobs for conformance runs    │
│  - Updates status subresource           │
│  - Exposes /healthz + /readyz probes    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
# Apply the CRD
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa/releases/latest/download/crd-conformancecheck.yaml

# Create namespace
kubectl create namespace cherenkov

# Deploy the operator
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa/releases/latest/download/operator-deployment.yaml
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa/releases/latest/download/operator-rbac.yaml

docs.title: Create a ConformanceCheck
docs.text:
apiVersion: validation.cherenkov.io/v1alpha1
kind: ConformanceCheck
metadata:
  name: my-api-check
spec:
  targetRef:
    apiVersion: v1
    kind: Service
    name: my-api
    namespace: default
    port: 8080
  specRef: https://my-api.example.com/openapi.json
  schedule: "0 */6 * * *"   # every 6 hours
  gates:
    - name: status-codes
      type: status
      assert: "all"
    - name: response-schema
      type: schema
      assert: "strict"
  llmConcurrency: 2
  failOnDrift: true

kubectl apply -f conformance-check.yaml
kubectl get conformancechecks
kubectl get cck  # short name

docs.title: spec fields
docs.text: Field Type Required Description targetRef object yes Reference to the target Kubernetes Service specRef string no URL or path to the OpenAPI spec schedule string no Cron expression for scheduled runs gates array no Conformance gates to enforce llmConcurrency integer no Max concurrent LLM tasks (1-16) deviceTargets array no Mobile device targets for visual testing visualConfig object no Visual validation configuration

docs.title: status fields
docs.text: Field Type Description phase string Pending, Running, Pass, Fail, or Error lastRun string ISO 8601 timestamp of last execution result object Pass/fail summary with divergence details conditions array Standard Kubernetes condition objects

docs.title: Operator Configuration
docs.text:
The operator Deployment exposes:

Endpoint Port Purpose /healthz 8081 Liveness probe /readyz 8081 Readiness + Ollama connectivity check Metrics 8080 Prometheus metrics

Environment variables:

Variable Default Description MAX_CONCURRENT_LLM_TASKS 2 Max parallel LLM calls per reconciliation

docs.title: RBAC
docs.text:
The operator uses a dedicated ServiceAccount (cherenkov-operator) with a ClusterRole granting access to:

  • conformancechecks + conformancechecks/status (CRD management)
  • jobs (batch execution)
  • pods, pods/exec, configmaps, events (runtime management)

docs.title: Building from Source
docs.text:
cd operator
docker build -t cherenkov-operator:latest .

The multi-stage Dockerfile produces a static binary (~20MB) that runs as non-root user 65532:65532.

For full source, see the operator directory and k8s manifests.

docs.title: Local LLM Setup
docs.text: CHERENKOV uses a local LLM by default. No cloud. No API keys. Your spec never leaves your machine.

docs.title: Default Setup (Ollama)
docs.text:
# Install Ollama
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Pull required models
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:7b    # Code generation (~4GB)
ollama pull deepseek-r1:8b      # Planning/reasoning (~5GB)

# Verify
ollama list

CHERENKOV will automatically detect and use Ollama at http://localhost:11434.

docs.title: Model Tiers
docs.text: Tier Default Model Use Case RAM Small qwen2.5-coder:7b Test code generation 8GB Deep deepseek-r1:8b Reasoning, planning 8GB Vision LocalAI VLM Screenshot analysis 8GB Cloud OpenAI/Anthropic Fallback API

docs.title: Configure via cherenkov.toml
docs.text:
[substrate]
default_tier = "small"

[substrate.ollama]
base_url = "http://localhost:11434"
small_model = "qwen2.5-coder:7b"
deep_model = "deepseek-r1:8b"

[substrate.localai]
base_url = "http://localhost:8080"
vision_model = "llava"

# Optional cloud fallback
[substrate.openai]
api_key = "${OPENAI_API_KEY}"
model = "gpt-4o"

docs.title: LocalAI (Vision Support)
docs.text:
LocalAI provides VLM (vision-language model) support for screenshot analysis:

# Start LocalAI via Docker
docker compose -f docker-compose.ai.yml up localai

# Verify
curl http://localhost:8080/v1/models

docs.title: Smaller Models (Low-RAM Machines)
docs.text:
# 4-bit quantized variants for 8GB RAM machines
ollama pull qwen2.5-coder:3b         # 2GB
ollama pull deepseek-r1:1.5b         # 1GB

# Update config

[substrate.ollama]
small_model = "qwen2.5-coder:3b"
deep_model = "deepseek-r1:1.5b"

Quality tradeoff

Smaller models generate valid but simpler tests. The 7B/8B defaults are recommended for best conformance coverage.

docs.title: Cloud Fallback (Optional)
docs.text:
export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

[substrate]
default_tier = "cloud"  # Force cloud for all tasks

CHERENKOV will route through OpenAI if local models are unavailable.

docs.title: OpenAPI Spec Integration
docs.text: CHERENKOV supports OpenAPI 3.x specifications in YAML or JSON format. The spec is the single source of truth for all conformance testing — endpoints, schemas, status codes, and constraints are all derived from it.

docs.title: Supported Formats
docs.text: Format Extension Notes OpenAPI 3.0 .yaml, .yml, .json Full support OpenAPI 3.1 .yaml, .yml, .json Full support (JSON Schema 2020-12)

docs.title: Point to Your Spec
docs.text:
# Local file
cherenkov validate --spec ./api/openapi.yaml --target http://localhost:8000

# Remote URL
cherenkov validate --spec https://example.com/openapi.json --target http://localhost:8000

# Read from stdin (pipe)
cat api.yaml | cherenkov validate --spec - --target http://localhost:8000

docs.title: What CHERENKOV Reads from the Spec
docs.text:
CHERENKOV extracts the following from your OpenAPI specification:

Element Used For Paths + methods Endpoint discovery and test generation Request schemas Request body and parameter validation Response schemas Response body type assertions Status codes Expected HTTP status per operation Parameters (path, query, header, cookie) Parameterized test scenarios Security schemes Authentication setup $ref references Resolved schema composition

docs.title: Spec Validation on Ingest
docs.text:
When you run cherenkov validate, the spec is validated before any tests are generated:

  1. Structure check — valid OpenAPI 3.x document
  2. Reference resolution — all $ref pointers resolve
  3. Schema coherence — no contradictory constraints
  4. Path uniqueness — no duplicate path+method combinations

If validation fails, CHERENKOV exits with code 2 and reports the specific errors.

docs.title: Tips for Spec Quality
docs.text:
• Use example fields — they help the LLM generate more realistic test data
  • Define required fields explicitly — CHERENKOV checks response bodies against these
  • Set minimum/maximum on numeric fields — enables boundary testing
  • Use enum for constrained values — tests will validate against allowed values
  • Include description on operations — the LLM uses this for test scenario planning

A well-annotated spec produces better conformance coverage:

paths:
  /pets:
    get:
      summary: List all pets
      description: Returns a paginated list of pets with optional filters
      parameters:
        - name: limit
          in: query
          schema:
            type: integer
            minimum: 1
            maximum: 100
            default: 20
      responses:
        '200':
          description: A list of pets
          content:
            application/json:
              schema:
                type: array
                items:
                  $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'

docs.title: Debugging Spec Issues
docs.text:
# Validate just the spec parsing without running tests
cherenkov doctor

# Generate tests only (no execution) to see what CHERENKOV extracts
cherenkov generate --spec api.yaml --output-dir ./tests

docs.title: Security Testing
docs.text: CHERENKOV includes embedded OWASP mutation payloads for lightweight DAST-style security testing.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
When running cherenkov validate, CHERENKOV automatically injects OWASP mutation payloads alongside conformance tests:

  • SQL injection strings in path/query parameters
  • XSS payloads in body fields
  • Oversized inputs for buffer testing
  • Invalid type coercions
  • Authorization boundary tests

docs.title: Enable Security Mutations
docs.text:
cherenkov validate \
  --spec api.yaml \
  --target http://localhost:8000 \
  --security-mutations \   # enable OWASP payloads
  --fail-on-drift

docs.title: SARIF Output
docs.text:
Security findings appear in the SARIF output and in the GitHub Security tab:

cherenkov validate --spec api.yaml --target http://localhost:8000 --output ./reports
# Produces reports/test-sarif.json

See SECURITY.md for the vulnerability disclosure policy.

docs.title: Test Generation & Repair
docs.text: CHERENKOV generates typed Playwright E2E tests from your OpenAPI spec using a local LLM. Each generated test goes through a 6-gate quality pipeline before it is written to disk. A repair loop automatically fixes failing tests — up to a configurable number of attempts.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Generate tests from an OpenAPI spec (with repair loop)
cherenkov generate --spec ./openapi.yaml

# Generate without repair — write first-pass results directly
cherenkov generate --spec ./openapi.yaml --no-repair

# Control the output directory
cherenkov generate --spec ./openapi.yaml --output-dir ./tests/generated

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A[OpenAPI Spec] --> B[Ingest Stage]
    B --> C[Plan Stage]
    C -->|"N scenarios"| D[AI Generator]

    D --> E{Repair enabled?}
    E -->|Yes| F["Generate -> Review -> Repair Loop\n(max-attempts iterations)"]
    E -->|No| G[Write first-pass result]

    F --> H[6-Gate Review]
    H -->|All pass| I[Write to disk]
    H -->|Gate fails + attempts remain| F
    H -->|Gate fails + no attempts left| J[Write best result so far]

    style A fill:#7c3aed,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
    style H fill:#db2777,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
    style I fill:#059669,stroke:#fff,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff

docs.title: cherenkov generate
docs.text: Flag Default Description --spec (required) Path to the OpenAPI spec (JSON or YAML) --output-dir stub/generated_tests Directory to write generated test files --repair / --no-repair --repair Enable or disable the generate-review-repair loop --max-attempts 3 Maximum repair iterations per scenario (1-10). Only used with --repair

docs.title: The 6-Gate Review Pipeline
docs.text:
Every generated test must pass six quality gates before CHERENKOV considers it production-worthy. The gates run in order; the first failure triggers a repair cycle (if enabled).

Gate What It Checks How 1. Syntax Valid JavaScript/TypeScript syntax Regex and structural checks 2. AST Correct test structure (describe/it blocks, expect calls) AST parsing 3. TypeScript Type-safe code that compiles tsc --noEmit via the stub project 4. Meaningful Assertion Test proves it catches a real bug, not just toBeTruthy() Checks for strict equality (toBe, toEqual) on response fields 5. Type-Check Response shape matches the spec schema Cross-references expect() targets against spec properties 6. Prism Dry-Run Test executes successfully against a Prism mock server Playwright execution against @stoplight/prism-cli

docs.title: Gate 4: Meaningful Assertion Gate
docs.text:
This gate is important enough to call out. A test that only checks expect(response.status).toBe(200) is trivially true — it does not prove the API works correctly. The meaningful assertion gate requires at least one assertion on the response body, using a strict comparator (toBe, toEqual, toStrictEqual).

This gate is controlled by the CHERENKOV_MEANINGFUL_ASSERTION_GATE environment variable (default: true).

// FAILS Gate 4 — no body assertion
test("GET /pets returns 200", async ({ request }) => {
  const response = await request.get("/pets");
  expect(response.status()).toBe(200);  // status-only = not meaningful
});

// PASSES Gate 4 — asserts on response body with strict comparator
test("GET /pets returns pets array", async ({ request }) => {
  const response = await request.get("/pets");
  const body = await response.json();
  expect(response.status()).toBe(200);
  expect(body[0].name).toBe("doggie");  // strict body assertion
});

docs.title: The Repair Loop
docs.text:
When --repair is enabled (the default), CHERENKOV uses a ChatTester-style loop:

  1. Generate — the LLM produces a test from the scenario
  2. Review — the 6-gate pipeline evaluates the test
  3. Repair — if a gate fails, the LLM receives the failure details and produces a corrected version
  4. Repeat — steps 2-3 repeat up to --max-attempts times
  5. Best result wins — if all attempts fail, the highest-quality version (most gates passed) is written to disk
# Allow up to 5 repair attempts for complex APIs
cherenkov generate --spec ./openapi.yaml --max-attempts 5

docs.title: Scenario Planning
docs.text:
Before generation begins, CHERENKOV plans test scenarios from the spec:

  • One file per scenario — each endpoint + method + mutation gets its own .spec.ts file
  • Naming convention — {METHOD}_{path}_{mutation_id}.spec.ts (e.g., POST_pets_happy_path.spec.ts)
  • Mutation types — happy path, unauthorized, invalid input, missing required fields, wrong content type

docs.title: Template Fallback
docs.text:
When no LLM is available (Ollama is down, or you pass --no-repair), CHERENKOV still generates tests using built-in templates. These templates produce structurally correct Playwright tests with placeholder assertions. They pass gates 1-3 (syntax, AST, TypeScript) but may not pass gates 4-6.

This makes CHERENKOV useful even offline or in environments where running an LLM is not practical — you get a working test skeleton that a human can refine.

docs.title: Confidence and HITL
docs.text:
After review, each test is assigned a confidence score:

Score Action >= 0.9 Auto-approved — written to disk directly 0.7 - 0.9 Routed to the HITL queue for human review < 0.7 Auto-rejected — not written to disk

docs.title: Output Structure
docs.text:
Generated tests land in --output-dir (default: stub/generated_tests/):

stub/generated_tests/
  GET_pets_happy_path.spec.ts
  GET_pets_petId_happy_path.spec.ts
  POST_pets_happy_path.spec.ts
  POST_pets_unauthorized.spec.ts
  POST_pets_invalid_body.spec.ts

Each file is a self-contained Playwright test that can be run independently:

cd stub
npx playwright test generated_tests/GET_pets_happy_path.spec.ts

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Check Suite (Integrity Audit) — verify generated tests have not been weakened
  • Human-in-the-Loop Workflow — review AI-generated tests that need human judgment
  • Configuration — configure LLM provider and model for generation
  • API Conformance Testing — the full validate pipeline that includes generation

docs.title: GitHub Actions Integration
docs.text:
CHERENKOV-QA provides a reusable GitHub Actions workflow template in the repository's .github/workflows/ directory. This is not a published GitHub Marketplace action -- copy the workflow into your own repository to use it.

Not a Marketplace action

The cherenkov-qa/action@v1 reference below is a template available in the CHERENKOV-QA repo's .github/workflows/ directory. Copy it into your project's .github/workflows/ and adjust paths as needed. A published Marketplace action is planned for a future release.

docs.title: Quick Setup
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/api-conformance.yml
name: API Conformance

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run CHERENKOV conformance
        uses: cherenkov-qa/action@v1
        with:
          spec: api/openapi.yaml
          target: http://localhost:8000
          fail-on-drift: true

docs.title: Action Inputs
docs.text: Input Required Default Description spec Yes — Path to OpenAPI spec target Yes — Base URL of server under test fail-on-drift No true Exit 1 on spec violation output No ./reports Report output directory python-version No 3.12 Python version

docs.title: Action Outputs
docs.text: Output Description drift-count Number of divergences found pass-rate Fraction of conformant endpoints report-path Path to the JUnit XML report sarif-path Path to the SARIF file

docs.title: Full Workflow with SARIF Security Tab
docs.text:
- name: Run CHERENKOV conformance
        uses: cherenkov-qa/action@v1
        id: conformance
        with:
          spec: api/openapi.yaml
          target: http://localhost:8000
          fail-on-drift: true
          output: ./reports

      - name: Upload test results
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: conformance-report
          path: reports/

      - name: Upload SARIF to Security tab
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: ${{ steps.conformance.outputs.sarif-path }}

      - name: Comment on PR with results
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            github.rest.issues.createComment({
              issue_number: context.issue.number,
              owner: context.repo.owner,
              repo: context.repo.repo,
              body: `**CHERENKOV Conformance:** ${{ steps.conformance.outputs.drift-count }} drift(s) found. Pass rate: ${{ steps.conformance.outputs.pass-rate }}`
            })

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• CI/CD Integration — GitLab CI, CircleCI, pre-commit, and the full pipeline flow
  • Check Suite (Integrity Audit) — add a test-integrity gate to your PR checks
  • Certificates & Compliance — attach a signed verdict to every green build
  • Configuration — environment variables for CI runners

docs.title: LangChain Integration
docs.text: CHERENKOV provides LangChain-compatible tools so you can embed API conformance testing inside AI agent workflows. An agent can generate tests, run validations, and explain violations — all as tool calls.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
langchain-core is a core dependency of CHERENKOV. Install it with the LangChain extras:

git clone https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa.git && cd cherenkov-qa
pip install -e .
pip install langchain-core

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from cherenkov.integrations.langchain.tools import CherenkovTool

# Create the tool — it wraps generate, validate, and explain actions
tool = CherenkovTool()

# Use it in a LangChain agent
from langchain_core.agents import AgentExecutor

agent = AgentExecutor(
    tools=[tool],
    # ... your agent config
)

docs.title: Available Actions
docs.text: The CherenkovTool is a single LangChain BaseTool that dispatches to different CHERENKOV actions based on the action parameter.

docs.title: generate_tests
docs.text:
Generate Playwright E2E tests from an OpenAPI specification.

result = tool._run(
    action="generate_tests",
    spec_path="./openapi.yaml",
    output_dir="./tests/generated"
)
Parameter Type Default Description spec_path str (required) Path to the OpenAPI spec (YAML or JSON) output_dir str stub/generated_tests Directory to save generated test files

docs.title: validate
docs.text:
Validate a live API against its OpenAPI specification.

result = tool._run(
    action="validate",
    target_url="http://localhost:8080",
    spec_path="./openapi.yaml",
    env="staging"
)
Parameter Type Default Description target_url str (required) URL of the API to validate spec_path str (required) Path to the OpenAPI spec env str dev Target environment label

docs.title: explain_violation
docs.text:
Get a natural-language explanation of a conformance violation.

result = tool._run(
    action="explain_violation",
    violation_id="GET /pets/{petId} returned 404 instead of 200",
    context="The pet was just created in the previous test"
)
Parameter Type Default Description violation_id str (required) The violation ID or message context str "" Additional context about the failure

docs.title: Using with a LangChain Agent
docs.text:
Here is a complete example that creates a LangChain agent capable of testing APIs:

from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.tools import BaseTool
from cherenkov.integrations.langchain.tools import CherenkovTool

# Create the CHERENKOV tool
cherenkov = CherenkovTool()

# Define a prompt that teaches the agent about CHERENKOV
prompt = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    ("system", """You are a QA assistant. You can:
    1. Generate tests from OpenAPI specs (action: generate_tests)
    2. Validate live APIs against specs (action: validate)
    3. Explain conformance violations (action: explain_violation)

    Always validate after generating tests to catch drift."""),
    ("human", "{input}"),
])

# Build the agent with your preferred LLM
from langchain_community.llms import Ollama

llm = Ollama(model="qwen2.5-coder:7b")

# Use with any LangChain agent framework
# (AgentExecutor, LangGraph, etc.)

docs.title: Input Schemas
docs.text:
The tool uses Pydantic models for input validation. These are available for type checking:

from cherenkov.integrations.langchain.tools import (
    GenerateTestsInput,
    ValidateInput,
    ExplainViolationInput,
)

# Use in typed code
input_data = GenerateTestsInput(
    spec_path="./openapi.yaml",
    output_dir="./tests"
)

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• Async not supported — CherenkovTool._arun() raises NotImplementedError. Use synchronous execution only.
  • Local execution — the tool runs CHERENKOV locally. The LLM provider configured in your environment (Ollama by default) must be available.
  • Single tool pattern — all three actions are bundled into one tool. This works well with most agents but may require explicit action routing in some frameworks.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Test Generation & Repair — understand what generate_tests does under the hood
  • API Conformance Testing — understand what validate does
  • MCP Integration — alternative integration via Model Context Protocol
  • Configuration — configure the LLM provider the tool uses

docs.title: MCP Ecosystem
docs.text: CHERENKOV ships a full Model Context Protocol (MCP) server with 41 tools and 6 resources.

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text:
The MCP server speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio — MCP clients spawn the process directly. There is no HTTP port to configure.

# Start the MCP server (stdio transport)
cherenkov mcp serve

docs.title: Available Tools (41)
docs.text:
Kept in sync with the code

This list is the exact tool set the server advertises via tools/list, mirrored 1:1 in the repository's manifest.json. Both are generated from cherenkov/mcp/handlers.py TOOLS.

docs.title: Conformance & Verification
docs.text: Tool Description run_conformance_check Run cherenkov validate against a target URL and return the report summary verify Probe a live server against its OpenAPI spec and return spec-drift divergences (cherenkov verify) verify_system Probe a live server against its OpenAPI spec; return spec-drift divergences as a VerificationReport verify_suite Run the 6-gate integrity check on an AI-generated test suite and return a VerificationReport validate_run_gate Run the Validation Gate and return a validate/v1 ValidationReport check_suite Static integrity check of a candidate suite vs. a baseline: catches WEAKENED, DELETED, HALLUCINATED assertions get_last_report Return the most recent .cherenkov/report.json without triggering a new run list_drift_findings Return structured spec-drift findings from the last conformance run get_tightening_suggestions Return OpenAPI spec tightening suggestions for a specific endpoint explain_finding Natural-language explanation of a specific drift finding using the LLM

docs.title: Generation & Healing
docs.text: Tool Description generate Generate Playwright E2E tests from an OpenAPI spec (cherenkov generate) auto_heal_code Generate a suggested code patch for a failed validation item (suggest-only)

docs.title: Test Integrity (IDE feedback)
docs.text: Tool Description cherenkov/audit-test-file Audit a test file for integrity issues: weakened assertions, tautological checks, spec mismatches cherenkov/check-assertion Quickly check whether a single test assertion line is strong or weak cherenkov/suggest-spec-fix Given an integrity issue in a test file, suggest a spec-anchored fix

docs.title: HITL Queue
docs.text: Tool Description hitl_list List HITL queue items matching the given status hitl_approve Approve a pending HITL item hitl_reject Reject a pending HITL item with reason

docs.title: Chat & Knowledge
docs.text: Tool Description chat_query_verdicts Query recent test verdicts from the Reflector chat_query_idioms Query learned idiom patterns from the Reflector chat_explain_divergence Explain a divergence using the Knowledge Mesh GraphRAG chat_run_test Plan test scenarios for a specific endpoint (suggest-only, does not execute) query_rag_index Query the SQLite RAG index for test historical artifacts

docs.title: Visual & Performance
docs.text: Tool Description visual_diff_baseline Run visual snapshot regression and UI matching checks visual_diff_baseline_enhanced Comprehensive visual regression with baseline management and configurable thresholds run_k6_perf Run K6 performance load testing and latency analysis

docs.title: Compliance & Governance
docs.text: Tool Description scan_mena_compliance Run MENA compliance localization and data residency checks scan_mena_compliance_enhanced Targeted MENA compliance checks (SAMA CCSF / Egypt CBE FinCSF) against a live API validate_governance_certification Validate a governance certification ID against quality standards report_compliance_findings Return structured compliance findings, filterable by severity/endpoint

docs.title: Export & Issue Tracking
docs.text: Tool Description export_jira_ticket Suggest-only Jira export for failed validation items export_linear_ticket Suggest-only Linear export for failed validation items export_github_ticket Suggest-only GitHub issue export for failed validation items

docs.title: Policy & Registry
docs.text: Tool Description policy_list List policy allow/block rules from cherenkov-policy.json policy_reload Reload cherenkov-policy.json from disk without restarting the server mcp_registry_list List all MCP servers registered in the mesh registry mcp_registry_publish Register an external MCP server with the mesh registry

docs.title: Event Bus
docs.text: Tool Description event_bus_list Fetch events from the UnifiedEventBus, optionally filtered by category event_bus_get Fetch a single event from the UnifiedEventBus by event_id event_bus_publish Publish a CHERENKOVEvent to the UnifiedEventBus for downstream consumers event_bus_stats Return UnifiedEventBus statistics (queue size, sink/source/handler counts, running state)

docs.title: MCP Resources (6)
docs.text: Resource URI Description HITL Pending Queue cherenkov://hitl/pending List of HITL items awaiting human review HITL Item Detail cherenkov://hitl/item/{id} Single HITL item by ID Latest Validation Report cherenkov://validate/latest Most recent validation report from the Validation Gate Validation Evidence cherenkov://validate/evidence Evidence files captured by the Validation Gate Active Chat Sessions cherenkov://chat/sessions List of active chat sessions Integrity Gates cherenkov://gates Machine-readable description of the 6 REVIEW gates

docs.title: Use with Claude Desktop / Cursor
docs.text:
Add to your MCP client config. The server is stdio, so the client launches it by command:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cherenkov": {
      "command": "cherenkov",
      "args": ["mcp", "serve"]
    }
  }
}

See cherenkov-mcp.yaml for the full MCP manifest.

docs.title: Slack & Teams Notifications
docs.text: CHERENKOV can send notifications to Slack, Microsoft Teams, and generic webhook endpoints when conformance events occur.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Configure notification endpoints in cherenkov.toml:

[notifications]
slack_webhook = "${SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL}"
teams_webhook = "${TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL}"

[notifications.triggers]
on_drift = true           # Notify when spec drift is detected
on_gate_fail = true       # Notify when CI gate fails
on_release = true         # Notify on new release

docs.title: Slack Setup
docs.text:
1. Create an Incoming Webhook in your Slack workspace:
  2. Go to https://api.slack.com/apps → Create New App → Incoming Webhooks
  3. Select the channel where alerts should appear

  4. Copy the webhook URL

  5. Set the webhook URL as an environment variable:

export SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL="https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00/B00/xxx"
  1. Run CHERENKOV — drift events will post to your Slack channel:

docs.title: Microsoft Teams Setup
docs.text:
1. In your Teams channel, click "..." → Connectors → Incoming Webhook → Configure
  2. Name the webhook and copy the URL
  3. Set the webhook URL:
export TEAMS_WEBHOOK_URL="https://outlook.office.com/webhook/xxx"

docs.title: Generic Webhook
docs.text:
Any HTTP endpoint can receive CHERENKOV notifications:

[notifications]
webhook_url = "${CUSTOM_WEBHOOK_URL}"

The payload format:

{
  "event": "drift_detected",
  "timestamp": "2026-06-29T12:00:00Z",
  "spec": "api.yaml",
  "target": "http://localhost:8000",
  "drift_count": 1,
  "findings": [
    {
      "endpoint": "GET /pets/{petId}",
      "expected": 200,
      "actual": 404,
      "evidence": "Field 'name' required but missing in response"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: CI/CD Integration
docs.text:
In CI pipelines, use the --output flag to generate reports that notifications can reference:

cherenkov validate --spec api.yaml --target http://localhost:8000 --fail-on-drift

When drift is detected and exit code 1 is returned, your CI system can trigger its own notification via Slack/GitHub/email using the JUnit XML or SARIF reports generated by --output ./reports.

docs.title: VS Code Extension
docs.text: The CHERENKOV-QA VS Code extension brings conformance testing directly into your editor.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
1. Open VS Code
  2. Press Ctrl+Shift+X (Extensions panel)
  3. Search for "CHERENKOV-QA"
  4. Click Install

Or install from the command line:

code --install-extension cherenkov-qa.cherenkov-vscode

docs.title: 11 Commands (Command Palette)
docs.text: Command Description CHERENKOV: Validate Run conformance check against target CHERENKOV: Generate Tests Generate tests from a spec file CHERENKOV: Eject Eject current tests to vanilla Playwright CHERENKOV: Open Dashboard Open the web dashboard CHERENKOV: Doctor Run environment diagnostics CHERENKOV: Init Initialize CHERENKOV in current workspace CHERENKOV: View Divergences Open conformance violations panel CHERENKOV: Approve Verdict Approve a HITL item CHERENKOV: Reject Verdict Reject a HITL item CHERENKOV: Memory Status Show knowledge mesh stats CHERENKOV: Knowledge Query Query the second brain

docs.title: Right-Click Integration
docs.text:
Right-click any .yaml or .json OpenAPI spec in the file explorer:

Right-click petstore.yaml → "Generate tests from this spec"

docs.title: Gutter Indicators
docs.text:
Endpoints in your spec file show live status indicators:

  • 🟢 Green dot — all tests passing
  • 🔴 Red dot — drift detected
  • ⚪ Grey dot — untested

docs.title: CodeLens
docs.text:
Above each path in your spec, see live test stats:

/pets:          ← [4 tests passing]
  get:          ← [✅ Conformant]
/pets/{petId}:  ← [1 conformance violation]
  get:          ← [❌ DRIFT: Expected 200, got 404]

Red squiggles appear on drifting endpoints. Press Ctrl+. for Quick Fix:

⚡ Apply suggested assertion for GET /pets/{petId}
⚡ Update spec: change expected status to 404
⚡ View full divergence report

The CHERENKOV sidebar shows a test explorer tree:

CHERENKOV
├── petstore.yaml
│   ├── ✅ GET /pets

docs.title: Release Notes: CHERENKOV-QA v1.0.0
docs.text:
Date: 2026-06-19 Tag: v1.0.0

We are thrilled to announce the v1.0.0 release of CHERENKOV-QA, the first AI-native API conformance testing engine.

docs.title: What is CHERENKOV?
docs.text: CHERENKOV reads your OpenAPI specification, uses a local LLM to generate typed Playwright API tests, executes them against a real server, and delivers conformance violation reports—all with zero vendor lock-in. If you want to leave CHERENKOV, a single eject command strips our framework and leaves you with vanilla, human-readable Playwright tests that run forever.

docs.title: Key Features in v1.0.0
docs.text: This release marks the completion of the Core API Track alongside 5 parallel extension tracks:

docs.title: 1. 🤖 Offline-First Local LLM Generation
docs.text:
• Defaults to qwen2.5-coder:7b for code generation.
  • No cloud dependencies. No API keys. Your spec never leaves your machine.
  • 6-gate review process (syntax, AST, TypeScript compilation, Prism mock) ensures generated tests are strictly valid.

docs.title: 2. 🔌 Zero Lock-In (cherenkov eject)
docs.text:
• Automatically compile generated tests into standalone Playwright specs.
  • Ejected tests use openapi-fetch and run without CHERENKOV dependencies.

docs.title: 3. 🎯 CI/CD Native Capabilities
docs.text:
• Fail-on-Drift Mode: Returns exit code 1 if the live server drifts from the OpenAPI spec.
  • JUnit XML & SARIF: Standardized reporting output formats for seamless CI/CD pipeline integrations and GitHub Security tab integration.
  • GitHub Action & Templates: Plug-and-play .gitlab-ci.yml and cherenkov-circleci-orb.yml available in the repository.

docs.title: 4. 📱 Multi-Platform Extension Tracks
docs.text:
• Desktop Host (Tauri): Fast native desktop wrapper (308MB payload) built in Rust.
  • Mobile Execution Core: Scaffolded Maestro and Appium device-flow runners.
  • Web Dashboard: Interactive React UI for visualizing execution results and divergence metrics.
  • K8s Operator: In-cluster scheduled conformance scanning.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: npx cherenkov-cli init

docs.title: Community and Next Steps
docs.text: We are entering the Reality Engine phase. Try CHERENKOV today to automate the tedious parts of QA, entirely locally. Join our Discord community, star the repository, and help us redefine API testing.

docs.text: Date: 2026-06-19 Tag: v1.1.0

docs.title: What's New Since v1.1.0
docs.text: v1.1.1 delivers 6 Claude Code-inspired enhancement phases (CC-1 through CC-6), 7 core platform phases (Phases 9-15), and numerous fixes.

docs.title: Claude Code-Inspired Enhancements
docs.text:
• CC-1 (Auto-Memory + Hooks): SQLite FTS5 memory engine, HookRegistry with 10 events, SubprocessHookExecutor. ADR-011, ADR-012.
  • CC-2 (Multi-Agent Conductor): Fan-out/fan-in orchestration over MCP mesh.
  • CC-3 (MCP Ecosystem): Marketplace, push events, JWT auth, 5 integrations.
  • CC-4 (Scheduling + Routines): APScheduler, web UI, GitHub webhook trigger.
  • CC-5 (Remote Control + Teleport): Session snapshots, QR-code join, remote runners.
  • CC-6 (CLI Composability): --json/--quiet on all commands, pipe mode, completions.

docs.title: Platform Phases
docs.text:
• Phase 9: Semantic Memory — MemSearch SDD integration.
  • Phase 10: CI/CD Native — Jenkins Shared Library.
  • Phase 11: VS Code Extension — full wiring.
  • Phase 12: gRPC Support — Buf Schema Registry.
  • Phase 13: Drift Reconciliation — L2 maker/checker.
  • Phase 14: Eval Pipeline — generate→grade→compare→optimize.
  • Phase 15: Synthetic Suite Generation — STORM-inspired multi-persona.

docs.title: New CLI Commands
docs.text:
• cherenkov demo — 60-second offline onboarding
  • cherenkov drift — spec-drift CLI with reconciliation
  • cherenkov report — divergence JSON summary + diff
  • cherenkov check-suite — AI cheating detection
  • cherenkov enterprise — enterprise-tier operations

docs.title: Other
docs.text:
• JWT + RBAC auth layer across all routes
  • Public documentation site (Material for MkDocs, GitHub Pages)
  • Coverage gap reporting (--coverage-report)
  • 8 P0 fixes across security, code quality, stability
  • Windows WSL SQLite UNC path handling

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Unprobed-endpoint reporting — cherenkov verify now lists every operation probe planning produced nothing for, with the real reason, before running. A zero-probe endpoint contributes no divergences, so a clean exit code previously implied coverage that never happened.
  • RecordingProxy — a forwarding HTTP proxy that records what a test suite actually receives from a live target, feeding a record-then-perturb audit that needs no known-honest baseline suite.
  • synthesize_mutant_battery() — emits one mutant per failure axis (status, single-value, enum, missing-field) plus a conforming control, so a test's failure is attributable to a specific weak assertion.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Soundness fix: verify could report a clean run on an endpoint it never probed, when a path parameter was declared once on the PathItem and inherited by every operation beneath it (a legal OpenAPI 3.x form). 11 regression tests added.
  • Misleading gate skip message — the mutant-synthesis skip reason now names the real cause instead of a generic "no documented success response."
  • Hanging unit test fixed — a mock that mocked nothing was opening a live LLM connection.

docs.title: Known issues (resolved in v1.2.0)
docs.text: • Release tags were inconsistent with the package version at this point in time — pyproject.toml declared 1.1.1 while the tag list already contained v1.2.0 and a malformed v.1.1.1. See the v1.2.0 release notes.

docs.title: UX Redesign
docs.text:
The web dashboard was reorganized around a 5-hub information architecture — Overview, Author & Generate, Triage, Coverage & Certification, and Knowledge — replacing the prior flat navigation. Alongside the restructure:

  • Triage moved to a Kanban board, with the "View Spec Diff" action wired to the real divergence detail.
  • Spec vs. Reality and Coverage & Certification now render live data from /api/v1/divergences instead of hardcoded samples; the certificate panel points to the cherenkov certify CLI rather than a fabricated history view.
  • Test Management is a new screen backed by real generated-test and run data, including a coverage/health trend chart.
  • Chat now lists real prior sessions (GET /api/v1/chat/sessions) instead of a placeholder history panel.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Release/tag reconciliation — .release-please-manifest.json and package.json had drifted to 1.0.0 while pyproject.toml and the actual tag history had already moved to 1.2.0, and the v1.1.1 release was tagged v.1.1.1 (stray dot), which breaks the docs-deploy version-extraction step. Manifest and package version now match; going forward, releases should be cut through release-please rather than hand-tagged to avoid a repeat.
  • Several runtime bugs surfaced by driving the app end-to-end in a real browser rather than relying on typecheck/build alone: an infinite Chat re-render loop, a missing Depends() wrapper causing 500s on the runs API, a non-JSON-serializable validation-error path, and duplicate React keys on the doctor/health checks list.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text: Phase 11 (VS Code extension) and Phase 12 (GraphQL/gRPC/AsyncAPI) are complete and wired in. Phase 13 (Enterprise: SAML/RBAC/audit/org/compliance) has real backend logic wired into cherenkov enterprise CLI commands (post-release, #810/#824). Phase 14's Spec Guardian daemon is now reachable via cherenkov guardian start (post-release, #811/#823). Phase 15 (fine-tuned model) is an explicit simulation, not a real training pipeline. Phase 16 (platform/marketplace) is mostly stub data. See the project issue tracker for current status per item — an earlier note here claimed all of Phase 11-16 was complete; that was inaccurate and has been corrected.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Spec Guardian CLI (Phase 14): cherenkov guardian start --spec <spec> --base-url <url> polls every endpoint declared in the OpenAPI spec and persists drift events to the drift store until interrupted (SIGINT/SIGTERM). Override with repeatable --endpoint METHOD:PATH, tune with --interval and --db. The SpecGuardianDaemon previously had zero callers; this gives it its first real entry point (#811, #823).
  • Enterprise CLI wiring (Phase 13): cherenkov enterprise commands now wire the real cherenkov/enterprise/ modules — SAML 2.0/SSO configuration, RBAC role assignment, org management, audit-log export, and SOC2 compliance reports — instead of the """Placeholder""" stubs that shipped in v1.2.0 (#810, #824).
  • MCP agent tools: check-suite, verify, and generate are exposed as agent-invokable MCP tools for IDEs/autonomous agents (#812, #821).
  • MCP registry manifest: manifest.json + publish instructions ready for submission to the official MCP registry (#792).
  • 5-Workspace UI/UX revamp (M1 prep): Overview, Author & Generate, Triage, Coverage & Certification, and Knowledge hubs; FastAPI backend wiring; a FastAPI SPA catch-all route; and a Playwright E2E suite (2e66658). The cold-run onboarding journey now survives end-to-end (session_a_zero_to_hero).
  • Scope filters: validate accepts a --tests filter and OpenAPI 3.0.x patch versions (#829).
  • Dual AI routing consolidation: the routing-layer analysis proposes a single tier-aware router, retiring the duplicate path (#815, #820).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Technical-debt pass (architecture review, #832): FTS5 query construction in knowledge/adapters/sqlite_repository.py and memory/adapters/sqlite_memory.py now joins on the FTS shadow-table rowid (avoiding a full-table scan) and escapes embedded quotes via a shared helper.
  • Generate persistence: test generation persists one distinct file per scenario (#828).
  • SDD runtime: agent_sync MemSearch workspace_dir API mismatch repaired (c7b2008).
  • OpenAPI version accept: validate accepts Swagger 2.0 and OpenAPI 3.0.x patch versions (#829).
  • M1 friction: resolve friction bugs across tests and UI automation (6c7335b).

docs.title: Certification
docs.text:
• Main certified green: 2064 passed / 2 failed. The 2 failures (test_verify_cmd.py, mock drift vs E0.5i known_identifiers/allow_mutations kwargs) are pre-existing and tracked as #819 (D7 — agents do not modify tests).
  • UI build verified: vite output matches the committed dist hashes; no frontend regression.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The malformed v.1.1.1 tag was corrected to v1.1.1. Release tags are now cut through release-please (via the release-please--branches--main branch) to avoid a repeat of the stray-dot breakage.
  • PAT expiry: the maintainer's gh PAT expired mid-session (patronizing GitHub Releases still works via SSH); renew ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml to restore gh/REST automation and to delete the ~110 stale claude/* agent branches.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Coverage Map API (Phase 14): build_coverage_map() in cherenkov/web/coverage_map.py computes per-endpoint conformance coverage from the in-process divergences corpus. Registered as GET /api/v1/coverage/map, returning endpoint tuples (method, path, status, last_run_id, last_verdict).
  • Continuous Conformance Trend (Phase 14): conformance_trend() and conformance_summary() stream verdict/divergence/coverage time-series from RunStore records. Registered as GET /api/v1/coverage/conformance-trend and GET /api/v1/coverage/conformance-summary (#767).
  • Regression Detection (Phase 14): detect_regressions() compares consecutive runs per target_url, flagging verdict_downgrade (PASS→FAIL), coverage_regression (pct drop), and divergence_spike (climb). Registered as GET /api/v1/coverage/regressions (#771).
  • PR-Comment Integration (Phase 14): format_coverage_comment() + GitHub client post a coverage-diff comment on opened/synchronize/reopened/ready_for_review events. Best-effort background task; never 5xxes the webhook (#766).
  • Consolidated Documentation 1.4: Unified 58-page Diátaxis documentation hierarchy, corrected version warning banner semantics, Mermaid version evolution flows, and static visual UI mockups.

docs.title: Design Notes
docs.text:
• Spec-derived (D7): verdict ranks are read from cherenkov/verdict/models.py (OverallVerdict: CERTIFIED/DIVERGENT/SUSPECT/INCONCLUSIVE), not hardcoded. Records sourced from RunStore (persistence/run_store.py); coverage map from the divergences corpus.
  • Eject-safe: coverage/conformance routes read only the public divergences and RunStore ports — eject strips CHERENKOV imports without breaking the contract.
  • Suggest-only healing: regression results are reports/suggestions; no auto-commit or auto-apply (D7 invariant maintained).

docs.title: Certification
docs.text:
• Conformance gate green at push: commit 4c5b4f2e — Automated Golden Path Validation Gate ✅ and CHERENKOV Conformance Tests ✅ both success.
  • New unit tests: 26 tests in tests/unit/test_coverage_map.py (including new TestDetectRegressions + TestRegressionsRoute), 26 passed in 2.66s.

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text:
You write APIs. You have an OpenAPI spec. You want to know — right now, on your machine — whether your implementation matches what the spec promises.

CHERENKOV gives you that answer in seconds, with zero cloud dependencies.

docs.title: 1. Install (30 seconds)
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa.git && cd cherenkov-qa
pip install -e .

docs.title: 2. Try the built-in demo (2 minutes)
docs.text:
No API server needed. CHERENKOV ships a demo that validates a bundled Petstore spec against a mock:

cherenkov demo

You will see generated Playwright tests, execution results, and a conformance summary — all local, all instant.

docs.title: 3. Validate your own API (3 minutes)
docs.text:
Point CHERENKOV at your spec and your running server:

cherenkov validate --spec openapi.yaml --target http://localhost:8000

CHERENKOV will:

  1. Parse your OpenAPI spec
  2. Generate Playwright tests for every endpoint
  3. Execute them against your live server
  4. Report conformant endpoints and drift

docs.title: 4. Check your health score (2 minutes)
docs.text:
cherenkov verify --url http://localhost:8000 --spec openapi.yaml

This runs spec-derived probes (40 by default) and returns a health score without generating full test files.

docs.title: 5. Check environment (1 minute)
docs.text:
cherenkov doctor

Confirms Ollama connectivity, spec readability, and target reachability.

docs.title: Quick Wins
docs.text: Time Command What you learn 30s cherenkov demo See CHERENKOV in action, no setup 60s cherenkov verify --url ... --spec ... Health score for your API 3m cherenkov validate --spec ... --target ... Full conformance report 5m cherenkov generate --spec ... Playwright tests in ./generated_tests/

docs.title: Local Validation Loop
docs.text:
This is the workflow you will use most. Think of it like running pytest — but the tests are generated from your spec.

flowchart TD
    A["Edit API code"] --> B["cherenkov validate\n--spec api.yaml\n--target localhost:8000"]
    B --> C{Drift?}
    C -->|"No"| D["Commit with confidence"]
    C -->|"Yes"| E["Review divergences"]
    E --> F["Fix implementation\nor update spec"]
    F --> A
# Full validation with detailed output
cherenkov validate --spec openapi.yaml --target http://localhost:8000

# Quick probe-only check (no test generation)
cherenkov verify --url http://localhost:8000 --spec openapi.yaml

When to use validate vs verify:

  • validate — generates and runs full Playwright tests. More thorough. Use before merging.
  • verify — sends spec-derived probes without generating test files. Faster. Use during active development.

docs.title: Generating Tests
docs.text:
Generate Playwright tests from your spec and keep them in your repo:

# Generate tests (uses local LLM by default)
cherenkov generate --spec openapi.yaml

# Generate without LLM (template fallback, no Ollama needed)
cherenkov generate --spec openapi.yaml --no-repair

# Generate and place in a specific directory
cherenkov generate --spec openapi.yaml --output-dir ./tests/conformance

Generated tests are standard Playwright — you can read them, edit them, run them with npx playwright test.

docs.title: Ejecting Tests
docs.text:
When you want full independence from CHERENKOV, eject your tests into standalone Playwright:

cherenkov eject --output ./tests

This strips all CHERENKOV imports and annotations, leaving pure Playwright tests you own completely. No lock-in. If CHERENKOV disappears tomorrow, your tests still run.

flowchart LR
    GEN["cherenkov generate"] --> TESTS["Generated Tests\n(CHERENKOV annotations)"]
    TESTS --> EJECT["cherenkov eject"]
    EJECT --> STANDALONE["Standalone Playwright\n(no dependencies)"]

docs.title: CI Integration (The Short Version)
docs.text:
Add a conformance gate to your pull requests:

# .github/workflows/conformance.yml
- name: API Conformance Check
  run: cherenkov validate --spec openapi.yaml --target http://localhost:8000
  # Exit code 0 = pass, 1 = drift detected (fails the build)

For the full CI/CD setup with Docker, caching, and parallel jobs, see the DevOps Guide.

docs.title: VS Code Integration
docs.text:
CHERENKOV integrates with VS Code for inline drift warnings:

  1. Install the CHERENKOV VS Code extension
  2. Open a project with an OpenAPI spec
  3. See inline annotations on endpoints that drift from spec

See VS Code Integration for full setup.

docs.title: Working Without an LLM
docs.text:
CHERENKOV's test generation uses a local LLM (Ollama) by default, but several commands need no LLM at all:

Command LLM needed? verify No check-suite No validate Yes (for generation) generate Yes (or use --no-repair for templates) eject No certify No doctor No

If you do not want to run Ollama, use generate --no-repair for template-based test generation, then run validate with pre-generated tests.

docs.title: Tips for Your Daily Workflow
docs.text:
Spec-first development. Write or update your OpenAPI spec before implementing. Then use cherenkov validate to confirm your implementation matches. This catches mismatches immediately instead of in production.

Use verify for fast feedback. During active coding, verify runs 40 probes in roughly 9 seconds. Use it like a linter — run it on save.

Commit generated tests. After cherenkov generate, commit the test files. They serve as living documentation of your API contract.

Eject when stable. Once an API surface stabilizes, eject the tests. You get permanent, dependency-free Playwright tests that document every contract.

docs.text:
You build pipelines and keep services running. You need CHERENKOV to fail builds on API drift, run in containers, deploy to Kubernetes, and emit telemetry your observability stack can consume.

This guide covers the infrastructure side — pipeline gates, container deployments, the K8s operator, and monitoring integrations.

docs.title: Quick Wins
docs.text: Time What Result 2m Add cherenkov validate to a CI step Builds fail on API drift 5m Run CHERENKOV in Docker No host dependencies 5m Add JUnit XML output to CI Drift shows in your test reporter 10m Deploy the K8s ConformanceCheck CRD Continuous in-cluster validation

docs.title: Exit Codes
docs.text:
Every CHERENKOV command uses consistent exit codes. Wire these into your pipeline logic:

Code Meaning 0 Pass — all conformant 1 Drift detected — one or more divergences 2 Configuration error 3 Configuration error (spec parse failure) 4 Network error (target unreachable)

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: API Conformance
on: [pull_request]

jobs:
  conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    services:
      ollama:
        image: ollama/ollama:latest
        ports:
          - 11434:11434
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install CHERENKOV
        run: |
          git clone https://github.com/moaidmoatasem/cherenkov-qa.git /tmp/cherenkov-qa
          pip install /tmp/cherenkov-qa

      - name: Start API server
        run: |
          # Start your API server in the background
          python -m your_api &
          sleep 5

      - name: Run conformance check
        run: |
          cherenkov validate \
            --spec openapi.yaml \
            --target http://localhost:8000

      - name: Upload JUnit results
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: conformance-results
          path: reports/junit.xml

docs.title: Without an LLM in CI
docs.text:
If you do not want to run Ollama in CI, use pre-generated tests:

      - name: Run pre-generated tests
        run: |
          cherenkov validate \
            --spec openapi.yaml \
            --target http://localhost:8000 \
            --tests ./tests/conformance

Or use verify for LLM-free probing:

      - name: API health check
        run: |
          cherenkov verify \
            --url http://localhost:8000 \
            --spec openapi.yaml

Or use check-suite to audit existing tests (no LLM, no running server):

      - name: Audit test suite
        run: |
          cherenkov check-suite \
            --candidate ./tests \
            --spec ./openapi.yaml \
            --fail-on-finding

Format Flag Use case JUnit XML --junit CI test reporters (GitHub, GitLab, Jenkins) SARIF --sarif GitHub Code Scanning, VS Code JSON --json Custom integrations, dashboards HTML --html Human-readable reports

version: "3.8"
services:
  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    ports:
      - "11434:11434"
    volumes:
      - ollama_data:/root/.ollama

        --spec /specs/openapi.yaml

docs.title: ConformanceCheck CRD
docs.text:
CHERENKOV provides a Kubernetes Custom Resource Definition for in-cluster conformance checking:

apiVersion: cherenkov.dev/v1alpha1
kind: ConformanceCheck
metadata:
  name: petstore-conformance
  namespace: default
spec:
  specRef:
    configMap: petstore-spec
    key: openapi.yaml
  target:
    service: petstore-api
    port: 8000
  schedule: "*/30 * * * *"    # Every 30 minutes
  failurePolicy: Alert        # Alert, Block, or Ignore
  reporters:
    - type: junit
      path: /reports/junit.xml
    - type: sarif
      path: /reports/conformance.sarif

docs.title: Deployment Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    subgraph cluster["Kubernetes Cluster"]
        CRD["ConformanceCheck CRD"] --> OPERATOR["CHERENKOV Operator"]
        OPERATOR --> JOB["CronJob\n(validation runs)"]
        JOB --> API["Your API Service"]
        JOB --> RESULTS["Results ConfigMap"]

    end

docs.text:
helm repo add cherenkov https://charts.cherenkov.dev
helm install cherenkov cherenkov/cherenkov-qa \
  --set spec.configMap=my-api-spec \
  --set target.service=my-api \
  --set target.port=8000 \
  --set schedule="*/30 * * * *"

See K8s Operator Guide for full CRD documentation.

docs.title: Daemon Mode
docs.text:
Run CHERENKOV as a long-lived process that periodically probes your API:

cherenkov daemon --url http://api.local:8000

In Docker or K8s, run the daemon as a sidecar or standalone deployment:

# K8s Deployment
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cherenkov-daemon
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: cherenkov
          image: cherenkov/cherenkov-qa:latest
          command: ["cherenkov", "daemon", "--url", "http://api-service:8000"]

docs.title: Spec Guardian
docs.text:
Monitor spec file changes and re-validate:

cherenkov guardian start --spec openapi.yaml --base-url http://localhost:8000

The guardian watches the spec file for changes (useful when specs are generated or synced from a schema registry).

docs.title: OpenTelemetry
docs.text:
CHERENKOV emits OpenTelemetry traces and metrics:

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
cherenkov validate --spec openapi.yaml --target http://localhost:8000

Metrics emitted:

  • cherenkov.validation.duration — time per validation run
  • cherenkov.validation.endpoints — endpoints tested
  • cherenkov.validation.drift — drift count per run
  • cherenkov.validation.health_score — overall health score

docs.title: Alerting
docs.text:
Combine daemon mode with your alerting stack:

flowchart LR
    DAEMON["cherenkov daemon"] --> OTEL["OTel Collector"]
    OTEL --> PROM["Prometheus"]
    PROM --> ALERT["Alertmanager"]
    ALERT --> SLACK["Slack / PagerDuty"]

docs.title: QA Engineer Guide
docs.text:
You own test quality. You need to know whether your test suite actually tests what the spec says — or whether assertions have been weakened, deleted, or hallucinated by an LLM.

CHERENKOV gives you a second opinion on every test in your suite, plus the tooling to triage, certify, and continuously monitor.

docs.title: The Spec-vs-Reality Problem
docs.text:
Most API test suites drift from the spec over time:

  • A developer weakens an assertion to make a flaky test pass
  • An LLM generates a test that checks the wrong status code
  • An endpoint changes but the test is not updated
  • A test is deleted and nobody notices

CHERENKOV catches all of these by comparing your tests against the OpenAPI spec as the source of truth.

flowchart TD
    SPEC["OpenAPI Spec\n(source of truth)"] --> CHERENKOV["CHERENKOV\ncheck-suite"]
    TESTS["Your Test Suite"] --> CHERENKOV
    CHERENKOV --> FINDINGS["Findings"]
    FINDINGS --> W["Weakened assertions"]
    FINDINGS --> D["Deleted coverage"]
    FINDINGS --> H["Hallucinated checks"]
    FINDINGS --> M["Missing endpoints"]

docs.title: Quick Wins
docs.text: Time Command What you learn 60s cherenkov check-suite --candidate ./tests --spec ./openapi.yaml How many findings in your suite 2m cherenkov verify --url ... --spec ... API health score (40 probes) 3m cherenkov dashboard Visual triage workspace 5m cherenkov certify Conformance certificate for this build

docs.title: 1. Audit Your Test Suite
docs.text:
check-suite is your primary tool. It reads your existing tests and compares them against the spec — no LLM needed, no network calls to your API:

cherenkov check-suite \
  --candidate ./tests \
  --spec ./openapi.yaml

The output categorizes findings:

  • Weakened — an assertion exists but checks less than the spec requires
  • Deleted — an endpoint in the spec has no corresponding test
  • Hallucinated — a test asserts something the spec does not define
  • Stale — a test references an endpoint or schema that no longer exists in the spec

docs.title: As a CI Gate
docs.text:
Fail the build if any findings exist:

cherenkov check-suite \
  --candidate ./tests \
  --spec ./openapi.yaml \
  --fail-on-finding

Exit code 1 means findings were detected. Wire this into your CI pipeline to prevent test quality regressions.

docs.title: 2. Triage with HITL Review
docs.text:
Not every finding requires action. CHERENKOV's human-in-the-loop (HITL) queue lets you triage:

# List pending findings
cherenkov hitl list

# Approve a finding (mark as intentional / accepted)
cherenkov hitl approve <finding-id>

# Reject a finding (flag for fix)
cherenkov hitl reject <finding-id>

Or use the Dashboard Triage workspace for a visual interface:

cherenkov dashboard
# Open http://localhost:8000 → Triage workspace

flowchart LR
    CS["check-suite\nfindings"] --> Q["HITL Queue"]
    Q --> APPROVE["Approve\n(intentional)"]
    Q --> REJECT["Reject\n(needs fix)"]
    APPROVE --> CERT["Conformance\nCertificate"]
    REJECT --> FIX["Developer\nfixes test"]
    FIX --> CS

docs.title: 3. Build Conformance Certificates
docs.text:
After triage, generate a conformance certificate that captures the state of your API:

cherenkov certify

The certificate includes:

  • Timestamp and spec version
  • Number of endpoints tested
  • Pass/fail breakdown
  • List of approved exceptions (from HITL)
  • Overall conformance score

Certificates are artifacts you can attach to releases, compliance reports, or audit trails.

docs.title: 4. Continuous Monitoring
docs.text: Set up ongoing conformance checks that catch drift as it happens:

docs.title: Daemon Mode
docs.text:
Run continuous validation on an interval:

cherenkov daemon --url http://localhost:8000

The daemon re-runs probes periodically and alerts on new drift.

docs.title: Spec Guardian
docs.text:
Watch for spec file changes and re-validate automatically:

cherenkov guardian start --spec openapi.yaml --base-url http://localhost:8000

The guardian monitors your spec file. When it changes, it re-validates and reports new drift.

flowchart TD
    subgraph continuous["Continuous Monitoring"]
        DAEMON["cherenkov daemon\n(periodic probes)"]
        GUARDIAN["cherenkov guardian\n(spec-change triggered)"]
    end
    DAEMON --> ALERT["Alert on drift"]
    GUARDIAN --> ALERT
    ALERT --> TRIAGE["Triage workspace"]
    TRIAGE --> FIX["Fix or accept"]

docs.title: The Full QA Workflow
docs.text:
Putting it all together for a release cycle:

flowchart TD
    A["Developer merges PR"] --> B["CI runs check-suite\n--fail-on-finding"]
    B -->|"Pass"| C["QA reviews dashboard"]
    B -->|"Fail"| D["PR blocked\n→ developer fixes"]
    C --> E["Triage HITL queue"]
    E --> F["cherenkov certify"]
    F --> G["Certificate attached\nto release"]
    G --> H["guardian monitors\nproduction"]
    H -->|"Drift detected"| I["New finding\nin HITL queue"]
    I --> E

docs.title: Reports
docs.text:
Manage and review conformance reports:

# List all reports
cherenkov report --list

# View the latest report
cherenkov report --run latest

# View a specific report
cherenkov report --run <run-id>

Reports include detailed per-endpoint results, timing data, and finding breakdowns.

docs.title: Tips for QA Engineers
docs.text:
Start with check-suite. It needs no LLM, no running server — just your tests and your spec. You will have findings within 60 seconds.

Do not auto-approve everything. The HITL queue exists because not every finding is a bug. Some are intentional deviations. Approve those explicitly so the certificate reflects conscious decisions.

Certify every release. Conformance certificates create an audit trail. When someone asks "was this API tested before release?", you have a timestamped, signed answer.

Combine check-suite with validate. check-suite audits your existing tests. validate generates and runs new tests. Together, they cover both "are our tests good?" and "does our API work?"

docs.title: What Does Not Need an LLM
docs.text:
As a QA engineer, most of your workflow is LLM-free:

Command LLM needed? check-suite No hitl list/approve/reject No certify No verify No daemon No guardian No report No

The only command that uses an LLM is generate (and validate, which calls generate internally). Everything in the audit-triage-certify workflow runs without Ollama.
